title: Trop v. Dulles
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Examines denationalization as punishment and the evolving-standards framework for cruel and unusual punishment.

title: Robinson v. California
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Addresses punishment of addiction status and application of the Cruel and Unusual Punishments Clause to states.

title: Estelle v. Gamble
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Introduces deliberate indifference to serious medical needs as an Eighth Amendment prison-care standard.

title: Farmer v. Brennan
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Explains deliberate indifference and prison officials' duties to protect people in custody from substantial risks of harm.

title: Hutto v. Finney
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Examines unconstitutional prison isolation conditions and the scope of remedial court orders.

title: Rhodes v. Chapman
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Analyzes prison overcrowding and the totality of conditions under the Eighth Amendment.

title: Solem v. Helm
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Develops proportionality analysis for a life-without-parole sentence; read alongside later decisions such as Harmelin.

title: Harmelin v. Michigan
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Presents the Court's divided treatment of proportionality and mandatory life sentences for adult noncapital crimes.

title: Atkins v. Virginia
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Addresses the constitutional prohibition on executing people with intellectual disability.

title: Roper v. Simmons
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Addresses the prohibition on capital punishment for offenses committed before age eighteen.

title: Graham v. Florida
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Examines juvenile life without parole for nonhomicide offenses and a meaningful opportunity for release.

title: Miller v. Alabama
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Addresses mandatory juvenile life-without-parole sentencing and individualized consideration of youth.

title: United States v. Bajakajian
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Explains gross disproportionality under the Excessive Fines Clause in a criminal forfeiture case.

title: McCulloch v. Maryland
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Foundational federalism context: discusses enumerated and implied national powers and state taxation of federal institutions.

title: United States v. Darby
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Explains the Tenth Amendment's relationship to federal commerce power in upholding labor standards.

title: National League of Cities v. Usery
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Historical decision limiting federal regulation of state employment; expressly overruled by Garcia in 1985.

title: Garcia v. San Antonio Metropolitan Transit Authority
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Overrules National League of Cities and examines political safeguards of state interests in federal regulation.

title: New York v. United States
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Develops anti-commandeering principles by examining federal directions to state legislatures over radioactive waste.

title: Printz v. United States
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Examines why Congress cannot compel state executive officers to administer federal background checks.

title: Reno v. Condon
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Distinguishes permissible regulation of state activities from commandeering in a driver-information privacy case.

title: Bond v. United States
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Addresses individual standing to challenge federal action on federalism and Tenth Amendment grounds.

title: National Federation of Independent Business v. Sebelius
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Federalism context: examines commerce power, taxation, and coercive conditions on state Medicaid funding.

title: South Dakota v. Dole
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Federalism context: analyzes constitutional limits on conditions attached to federal highway funds.

title: Hodel v. Virginia Surface Mining and Reclamation Association
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Examines cooperative federal regulation and claims that mining standards impair state sovereignty.

title: FERC v. Mississippi
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Examines federal energy regulation and state regulatory procedures under the Tenth Amendment.

title: Griswold v. Connecticut
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Addresses marital privacy; Justice Goldberg's concurrence discusses the Ninth Amendment, distinct from the majority's reasoning.

title: United Public Workers v. Mitchell
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Includes the Court's treatment of Ninth and Tenth Amendment objections to federal restrictions on political activity.

title: Troxel v. Granville
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Contextual Fourteenth Amendment parental-rights decision; Justice Scalia discusses the Ninth Amendment in dissent, not a Ninth Amendment holding.

title: Washington v. Glucksberg
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Contextual substantive-due-process decision on asserted unenumerated rights and assisted suicide, not a Ninth Amendment holding.

title: Lawrence v. Texas
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Contextual Fourteenth Amendment liberty decision concerning adult intimacy, not a holding creating a Ninth Amendment cause of action.

title: Meyer v. Nebraska
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Contextual Fourteenth Amendment liberty decision about language education and family choices, not a Ninth Amendment holding.

title: Pierce v. Society of Sisters
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States / Library of Congress
description: Contextual Fourteenth Amendment decision about parental educational choices, not a Ninth Amendment holding.

title: Timbs v. Indiana
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States
description: Addresses incorporation of the Excessive Fines Clause against state governments.

title: Murphy v. National Collegiate Athletic Association
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States
description: Explains anti-commandeering and distinguishes federal preemption from instructions to state legislatures.

title: Haaland v. Brackeen
publisher: Supreme Court of the United States
description: Examines congressional authority and anti-commandeering challenges involving the Indian Child Welfare Act.

title: Constitution Annotated: Eighth Amendment - Further Guarantees in Criminal Cases
publisher: Congressional Research Service / Government Publishing Office
description: Official 2016 analysis of the 8th Amendment and its judicial interpretation; a dated research reference, not a continuously updated edition.

title: Constitution Annotated: Ninth Amendment - Unenumerated Rights
publisher: Congressional Research Service / Government Publishing Office
description: Official 2016 analysis of the 9th Amendment and its judicial interpretation; a dated research reference, not a continuously updated edition.

title: Constitution Annotated: Tenth Amendment - Reserved Powers
publisher: Congressional Research Service / Government Publishing Office
description: Official 2016 analysis of the 10th Amendment and its judicial interpretation; a dated research reference, not a continuously updated edition.

publisher: University of Chicago Law Review Dialogue
description: Kurt Lash examines competing views of the Ninth Amendment and judicial enforcement of privacy rights.

title: Reviving Elusive Rights: State Constitutional Unenumerated Rights Clauses as Bounded Guarantors of Fundamental Liberties
publisher: Georgetown Journal of Law & Public Policy
description: Comparative context: examines state unenumerated-rights clauses and their relationship to Ninth Amendment interpretive debates.

title: The Ninth Amendment: The Hard Problem of U.S. Constitutional Law
publisher: University of Pittsburgh Law Review
description: Jorge Farinacci-Fernos examines several possible functions of the Ninth Amendment after Dobbs.

title: Baby Ninth Amendments and Unenumerated Individual Rights in State Constitutions Before the Civil War
publisher: Mercer Law Review / Northwestern University Law Review repository
description: Comparative scholarship traces state clauses inspired by the Ninth Amendment and their protection of unenumerated rights.

title: Natural Rights and the Ninth Amendment: How Does Lockean Legal Theory Assist in Interpretation?
publisher: NYU Journal of Law & Liberty
description: Michael McConnell examines retained natural rights and the Ninth Amendment through Lockean legal theory.

title: The Golden Mean Between Kurt & Dan: A Moderate Reading of the Ninth Amendment
publisher: Drake Law Review
description: Randy Barnett contrasts competing Ninth Amendment theories and argues for protection of fundamental liberties.

title: Three Myths of the Ninth Amendment
publisher: Drake Law Review
description: Kurt Lash challenges common individual-rights and historical assumptions about the Ninth Amendment.
